tasks.title: Build a customer list, filter and edit journey
tasks.prompt: In the supplied React consumer fixture, build the customer-management screen from the frozen brief and realistic customer data. Users must browse, filter, create and edit customers. Include the brief's loading, empty, error, success, submitting and denied-operation states and the specified recovery actions. Preserve the supplied design tokens. The evaluator runs the production build and independent checks after the autonomous attempt.

checks.description: An evaluator-observed production build exits successfully in the declared consumer environment.
Independent browser assertions complete the task's stated list, filter and edit or maintenance outcomes.
Independent browser assertions cover each required loading, empty, error, success, submitting and permission state relevant to the task, including recovery.
Independent keyboard assertions verify named controls, focus order, dialog entry/return and completion of the required interaction without a pointer.
Independent assertions at 390 px and 1280 px verify readable required content, reachable actions and no unintended horizontal page overflow.
A reviewer independent of the agent and intervention assesses information hierarchy, task clarity and realistic copy against the frozen task rubric.

design.repetitionUnit: An independently started autonomous attempt for one condition and task in a fresh workspace; every condition-task cell requires at least minimumAttempts observations.
design.schedule: Seeded random permutation of condition-task-repetition assignments; freeze the complete createSchedule output in the cohort manifest before observing outcomes. Real attempts must match their assigned cohort/condition/task/repetition/order exactly. Available cells may run while planned cells remain planned.
design.cohortManifest: cohorts.json in the evidence root is an array of frozen manifests with schemaVersion 2, cohortId, protocolSha256 from canonical protocolDigest(protocol), pins {commit, documentationSha256, registrySha256, rubricSha256, browser {name, version}}, the complete createSchedule output as schedule, and controls {host, model, environment, versions, budget, capabilities {network, shell, mcp}, fixtures [{id, sha256}]}. See cohort.schema.json. Without a manifest, assignment coverage is unverified and the report can never be pilot-ready.
design.control: Freeze controls before the first outcome: host {name, version}, model {name, version, versionKind}, environment {os, node}, versions {registry, cli, mcp, toolSchema}, budget {elapsedMs, toolCalls, inputBytes, outputBytes, tokens}, Boolean capabilities {network, shell, mcp}, and exactly every protocol fixture ID once with its actual SHA-256 digest. All observations, including the first, must match the pre-frozen controls; mismatches reject. Changed controls require a separate frozen cohort. Keep aliases labelled as aliases when no immutable model version exists; freeze documentation and task/rubric revisions before collecting outcomes.
design.toolVersions: Each attempt records the actual CLI/MCP and intervention tool/schema versions. Do not substitute a planned condition with the existing workflow; record unavailable conditions as pending.
design.freshWorkspaceRule: Create a unique workspace from the pinned initial task fixture for every attempt. Do not reuse artifacts, transcripts, failure feedback or agent context from a previous attempt.
design.failures: Retain assigned attempts, failures, timeouts, budget exhaustion and partial artifacts. Do not replace unsuccessful runs or publish only the best outcome.
design.assistance: A human-assisted rescue remains a failed primary assignment and also appears in the assisted stratum. Preserve pre-rescue evidence as hashed artifacts; primary autonomous usage is unavailable for assisted records. Positive correction counts require hashed reason artifact references. Normal source customization is not automatically a defect.
design.independence: The agent's self-report and intervention review engine cannot supply the sole acceptance verdict. Build/browser evidence is produced by the trusted evaluator; human design evidence comes from an independent reviewer.
design.humanReview: Use a frozen hierarchy, task-clarity and copy rubric with condition-blinded artifact identifiers where practical. Record when treatment could not be concealed. Participant contact requires applicable authorization.
design.heldOut: Reserve the transfer fixture, brief and assertion bodies outside tool-authoring examples. Freeze intervention code, schemas and rubrics before revealing held-out evidence; record any exposure.
design.evidence: Store bounded attempt records and relative SHA-256 artifact references. Redact secrets, personal data and private paths before evidence ingestion/publication. Published transcripts retain provenance without private filesystem paths.
design.missingMetrics: Missing elapsed time, calls or input/output byte usage makes budgetStatus unknown and cannot be accepted. A numeric token budget requires measured token usage; unavailable tokens are permitted without blocking acceptance only when the token budget is unavailable. Missing instrumentation is never zero. Failed, missing or unknown required checks cannot count as autonomous success.
design.primaryOutcome: Autonomous successes divided by every frozen assignment in each available condition-task cell, including retained failures/timeouts, missing outcomes and human-assisted rescues. Missing outcomes remain pending; planned assignments remain planned with no rate. Complete success requires every required independent check and budget to pass with no human correction.
design.summary: Report assigned, observed, missing and planned counts, primary success denominator, observed profile summaries and median/minimum/maximum of available measurements; report unavailable counts and every failure. Without frozen cohorts.json, only observed counts are available, assignment coverage is unverified and pilot readiness is impossible. Empty cells remain pending without invented numeric outcomes.
design.interpretation: At least five attempts per condition/task is a pilot threshold, not a broad statistical claim. Cross-registry comparisons require a separate protocol controlling unequal catalogs and functionality.
design.executionBoundary: The v2 tooling validates evidence and generates a schedule/report; it does not invoke an agent, execute submitted source or run paid models. Independent consumer/browser evaluators are separate trusted work and remain pending.
design.authorization: Do not launch paid model runs or contact participants without applicable authorization. No telemetry or arbitrary remote code is part of this protocol.
